title: PRD: Compliance-gated launch for hosted inference surface with tenant isolation and audit gates
creator: Asha Patel
description: Objective: deliver a production-grade hosted API surface for generation (chat/completions), embeddings, and rerank that meets enterprise compliance requirements for auditability, tenant isolation, and data residency. This PRD clarifies scope changes requested by sales/legal, defines acceptance gates that are compliance-driven, and lists a tactical launch checklist designed to unblock go/no-go decisions for customers in regulated industries. Out of scope: private/VPC packaging, Dedicated SLA contracts (covered in a follow-up PRD).
scope_clarifications: Behavioral compatibility: responses should match existing hosted contract for default models; non-deterministic differences documented in release notes
Tenant isolation: logical tenant isolation on the control plane and per-tenant telemetry. No hardware-level single-tenant guarantees in this launch.
Audit logging: record API request metadata, model id, model version, tenant id, timestamps, routing decision, and fallback events. Stored for 180 days by default.
Encryption: data in transit TLS1.3, data at rest encrypted via KMS; KMS integration for customer-managed keys is included for launch for selected enterprise customers (gradual roll-out).
Data residency: regional routing by tenant with opt-in residency assignment. Initial support for NA and EU regions only.
acceptance_criteria: API Contract: all four endpoints conform to OpenAPI spec v1.2 in the docs with examples and error codes

Audit Logs: every production request contains required fields (tenant_id, request_id, model_id, model_version, routing_node, outcome). Audit log ingestion validated in staging and spot-checked in production for 7 days
RBAC: console access and API token issuance support tenant-scoped roles (admin, auditor, billing). RBAC flows exercised end-to-end by solutions engineering
KMS: ability to encrypt customer data via customer-managed KMS keys for at least two pilot customers; documentation and test harness available
Traffic Isolation: per-tenant burst and soft-quota enforcement works for 95th percentile traffic profiles without cross-tenant interference
Telemetry: latency, p50/p95/p99, error-rate, cost-per-1k-tokens, and model-fallback counts are tracked per-tenant and visible in the Console dashboards
Safety Gates: eval suite passes for 99% of gated prompt-set checks for initial launch models; any regression(s) are tied to rollback playbook
Canary: canary slice (1% of traffic) yields no critical SLO violations for 72 hours before gradual ramp to 25% and then to 100%
Operational Runbook: incident playbook with rollback, fallback to safe-model lane, and customer-notification templates published
Security Review: third-party security review and internal security checklist completed and signed off
launch_checklist: Finalize API docs and SDK examples for all four endpoints
Complete audit-log ingestion pipeline and retention policy tests
Enable tenant-scoped RBAC in Console and test user flows
Enable KMS integration for two pilot tenants and validate key lifecycle operations
Wire per-tenant quotas/burst controls and simulate noisy-neighbor scenarios
Create Console dashboard tile: tenant telemetry (latency, errors, cost) and model-fallback heatmap
Run eval harness across seeded prompt-sets; document regressions and remediation
Prepare rollback playbook and postmortem templates; schedule tabletop exercise with SRE and Customer Success
Create migration docs and deprecation notices for customers expecting older behavior
Prepare customer-facing compliance pack (SLA addendum, audit log schema, KMS setup guide)
Legal sign-off on data residency language and retention durations
Security final review and penetration test sign-off
Set canary routing policy and monitoring alerts; predefine thresholds and alert channels
Coordinate support rotations and on-call escalation matrix for first 4 weeks of launch
Create GitHub release with changelog, migration notes, and SDK bump commits
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Internal dogfood (7 days): enable full stack for internal tenants and Red team; fix critical telemetry gaps
Phase 1 - Pilot customers (2 customers, 2 weeks): enable KMS and tenant isolation for pilots with assigned SRE and Solutions Engineer
Phase 2 - Canary public (1% traffic, 72h): monitor SLOs and audit logs; trigger rollback on critical violations
Phase 3 - Ramp to 25% (48h hold after canary): verify multi-tenant telemetry and quota enforcement
Phase 4 - Full roll (staged by region): open signups, enable Console features, and start billing cadence
telemetry_and_kpis: Token cost per 1k: baseline and target reduction after optimizer rules
Latency: p50/p95/p99 for each endpoint by tenant tier
Model-fallback rate: track % of requests that fall back to lower-tier model
Audit-log completeness: percent of requests with fully populated audit records
Quota enforcement efficacy: percent of quota violations correctly throttled
api_contract_changes: Add 'tenant_id' header as required for enterprise-tenanted calls (backwards compatible when absent for legacy tenants)
New error code 429-TENANT-BURST for tenant-level burst throttling responses
Audit metadata returned in response header X-RW-AUDIT-ID to correlate client and server logs
Model-version pinning supported via 'model_version' query param; documented semantics for fallback and deprecation
migration_notes: Legacy tokens will continue to work but will be flagged in Console and customers will be asked to opt into tenant-scoped tokens
Customers with strict residency requirements must opt-in; default routing remains global until residency is configured
SDKs will expose tenant-scoped helpers; migration guide includes curl examples and Node/Python snippets
